Rashi on Eruvin 10a:10:1.english: Because Rabbi Ḥiyya taught in accordance with him - [In the baraita:] "A wall, one side of which is recessed, etc."

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:11:1.english: Up to how much - May it be wide and not need to be reduced, according to Rabbi Yehuda?

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:13:1.hebrew: פסי ביראות שהתרתה בהן - שלש עשרה אמה ושליש, דתנן בפרק שני (לקמן עירובין יז:) עושין פסין לביראות שברשות הרבים, והן עמוקין עשרה, ואסור למלאות מהן ולהניח על שפתן, שמוציא מרשות היחיד לרשות הרבים. והתירו חכמים לעשות ארבעה דיומדין לארבע פיאות, ולשוויה בין הפסין רשות היחיד, ומותר למלאות. ושרי רבי יהודה להרחיק זה מזה מלא שני רבקות של ארבעה ארבעה בקר, ועוביה של פרה אמה ושני שלישי אמה, דהוו להו שלש עשרה אמה ושליש לשמונה בקר:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:13:1.english: Boards surrounding wells, where you permitted within them - [Namely,] thirteen cubits and a third, as we learned in the second chapter (below, Eruvin 17b): One may make boards for wells that are in the public domain and are ten [handbreadths] deep, and it is forbidden to draw [water] from them and place [it] on their rim, for one carries out from a private domain into a public domain. And the Sages permitted making four double posts for the four corners, and rendering [the area] between the boards a private domain, so that it is permitted to draw [water]. And Rabbi Yehuda permits distancing [them] from one another the full [measure of] two teams of four cattle each; and the breadth of a cow is a cubit and two-thirds of a cubit, which comes out to thirteen cubits and a third for eight cattle.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:14:1.hebrew: והיא הנותנת - מדה זו שאתה מביא בה איסור ליותר משלש עשרה אמה ושליש למבוי, משום טעמא דלא התרתה בו פרוץ מרובה על העומד, היא הנותנת טעם להיתר: דהתם הוא דאיכא עומד מועט, משום הכי לא התרתה בו יותר משלש עשרה אמה ושליש; אבל מבוי דרובו סתום, שרי ביה טפי:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:14:1.english: And that is what provides [the reason] - This principle through which you derive a prohibition for [an entrance of] more than thirteen and a third cubits in an alleyway, on the grounds that you did not permit in it [a partition where] the breached [portion] exceeds the standing [portion], is that which provides a reason for permission: For it is there [regarding well-boards] that there is [only] a small amount of standing [partition], which is why you did not permit in it [an opening of] more than thirteen and a third cubits; but an alleyway, whose majority is closed [by walls], is permitted [to have an entrance] even wider.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:15:1.hebrew: אי נמי לאידך גיסא - דלא תיתי ליה מפסי ביראות: דאילו התם הוא דהקלת בה קולא, דמכשרת ליה בפרוץ מרובה על העומד, אקיל נמי קולא אחריתא, דלהוי חשוב פתח עד שלש עשרה אמה ושליש:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:15:1.english: Alternatively, to the other side - So that it cannot be derived from [the case of] boards surrounding a well: For whereas there you applied a leniency, in that you validated it [even where] the breached [portion] exceeds the standing [portion], apply another leniency as well, that [an opening of] up to thirteen and a third cubits should be considered an entrance.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:15:2.english: Not at all - More than ten [cubits is] not [permitted].

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:16:1.english: The halakha is not in accordance with that teaching - Because the airspace on this side and on that side comes and nullifies the reed.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:1:1.english: It is Rabbi, who said we require - Two remaining sections [of wall] for a courtyard of ten [cubits] that was breached in its entirety.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:1:2.hebrew: חצר ניתרת בפס אחד - אם נפרצה לרשות הרבים, ונשתייר בה מצד א', מותרת. ובשאין הפירצה יותר מעשר עסקינן, דאי יותר מעשר, לא מהני ליה מחיצה להאי חצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:1:2.english: A courtyard is permitted with one post - If it was breached into the public domain and [a remnant] remained of it on one side, it is permitted. And we are dealing with [a case] where the breach is no more than ten [cubits], for if [it is] more than ten [cubits], a partition does not avail for this courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:2:1.hebrew: האי מאי אי אמרת בשלמא - מתני', כדהוה שמעינן לה מעיקרא: במכוונת קטנה כנגד אמצעיתה של גדולה, ומהאמה היתירה נשארו שלשה לכאן ושלשה לכאן, וי"ל נראה מבחוץ ושוה מבפנים משני רוחות, ואפילו הכי קטנה אסורה, דנראה מבחוץ ושוה מבפנים לא מהני. ורבי בשני פסין דחצר כרבי יוסי סבר לה, דאמר במתני': אין לחי פחות מרוחב שלשה, וכל שכן פסין דחצר, דבעי רוחב כדבעי רבי יוסי בלחי:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:2:1.english: What is this? Granted, if you say - The mishna is [explained] as we initially understood it: where the small [courtyard] is aligned opposite the middle of the large [courtyard], and from the extra cubit, three [handbreadths] remained on this side and three on that side. And one can say [that it is] visible from the outside and even from the inside on both sides, and even so, the small [courtyard] is forbidden, because [a partition that is] visible from the outside and even from the inside is not effective. And Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], regarding the two posts of a courtyard, holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who said in the mishna: A side post is not less than a width of three [handbreadths]; and all the more so the posts of a courtyard, which require width just as Rabbi Yosei requires for a side post.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:2:2.hebrew: ודרבינא - דאוקמא במופלגין, מזה בשנים ומזה בארבעה, ליתא; דא"כ, לא הוה משתריא גדולה, דפס ב' טפחים לא מהני. וכיון דליתא לדרבינא, ליתא נמי לדרבי זירא דאוקמא בנכנסין; דכיון דמכוונת, שלשה מכאן ושלשה מכאן, כניסה מאי מהניא? הא כי נכנסין נמי איכא למשרייה בנראה מבחוץ ושוה מבפנים משתי רוחות, ולא שרינן לה, דמוקמינן ליה בנראה מבחוץ ושוה מבפנים אינו נידון משום לחי. משום הכי יהיב תנא שיעור לעודפה של גדולה, שתהא יתירה על הקטנה אמה, כי היכי דניהוו לה לגדולה שלשה מכאן ושלשה מכאן, משום דרבי שני פסין בעי, ורחבי' שלשה כרבי יוסי, ומשום היתר גדולה נקט לה:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:2:2.english: And [the explanation] of Ravina - That he established it where [the walls] are spaced apart, on this side by two [handbreadths] and on that side by four [handbreadths], is not [accepted]; for if so, the large [courtyard] would not be permitted, as a board of two handbreadths is not effective. And since Ravina's [explanation] is not [accepted], Rabbi Zeira's [explanation]—who established it where [the small courtyard's walls] enter [recessed]—is also not [accepted]. For since it is centered, [leaving] three [handbreadths] on this side and three [handbreadths] on that side, what does entering [being recessed] accomplish? Behold, even when they enter, it would be possible to permit it [the small courtyard] based on [the rule of] "visible from the outside and flush from the inside" from both directions, yet we do not permit it, because we establish it that [a post that is] visible from the outside and flush from the inside is not judged as a side post. Therefore, the Tanna gave a measure for the excess of the large [courtyard], that it be greater than the small one by a cubit, so that there will be for the large [courtyard] three [handbreadths of wall remaining] on this side and three [handbreadths] on that side, because Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] requires two posts, and their width [must be] three [handbreadths], like Rabbi Yosei; and [it was] for the sake of permitting the large [courtyard that he] formulated it.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:3:1.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת נראה מבחוץ - מהני, וקטנה דאסירא, היינו טעמא: משום דאיתא לדרבי זירא בנכנסין ולדרבינא במופלגין, וליכא לבוד משני רוחות. ואפילו הכי, גדולה משתריא בגיפופין הנשארין לה מאחורי הכניסות, ואף על פי שרוחב האחד אינו אלא ב' טפחים, דלא סבר לה כר' יוסי:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:3:1.english: However, if you say [that a post that is] visible from the outside - is effective [as a side post]; and [as for the fact] that the small [courtyard] is forbidden, this is the reason: because [the explanation] of Rabbi Zeira where [the walls] enter [recessed] and [the explanation] of Ravina where [the walls] are spaced apart are [accepted], and there is no lavud from both sides; and even so, the large [courtyard] is permitted through the wall projections remaining for it behind the recesses, even though the width of one [of them] is only two handbreadths, for [Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi] does not hold in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:3:2.english: The large [courtyard is] eleven [cubits] - That the Tanna gave a measure of a cubit for its excess — why do I need [this]?

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:4:1.english: If [it is] to permit the large [courtyard] - It comes [to teach] that it should have a remainder [of wall] on both sides.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:4:2.english: Ten [cubits] and two handbreadths suffices - For Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Yose.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:4:3.hebrew: ואי למיסרה לקטנה קאתי - כדי שירחקו כותלי אורך הגדולה מכניסתה של קטנה ד' טפחים מצד האחד, דלא לימצי למימר לבוד למשרייה, ולאגמוריה דאי לאו הכי, הוה שרינן לה בקטנה בנראה מבחוץ על ידי לבוד:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:4:3.english: And if it is coming to prohibit the small [courtyard] - In order that the length walls of the large [courtyard] be distant from the entrance of the small [courtyard] by four handbreadths on one side, so that one cannot say [that] lavud [applies] to permit it, and to teach us that were it not so, we would permit the small [courtyard] through [a post that is] visible from the outside by means of lavud.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:4:4.hebrew: לישמעינן - גדולה רחבה הרבה ומיפלגי טובא, דהוי מילתא דפסיקא. דהא לאו מילתא דפסיקא היא, הואיל ומופלג' מכותל זה בשלשה ומכותל זה בשלשה. ואי הגדולה רחבה הרבה הוה תני, הוה גמרינן מינה טפי דמשום הפלגה מיתסרא. והא ליכא למימר דדק תנא בשיעורין לאשמועינן דבהכי הוא דמיתסרא ובבציר מהכי לא, דהא בי' וד' טפחים נמי מיתסרא, וכגון דמופלגת בחצי טפח מכאן ובשלשה וחצי מכאן, דמשתריא גדולה בגיפוף משהו מכאן ושלשה וחצי מכאן, וקטנה מיתסרא, דליכא לבוד משני רוחות:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:4:4.english: Let it teach us - [That] the large [courtyard] is much wider and they are very far separated, so that it would be a clear-cut case. For this is not a clear-cut case, since [here] it is separated from this wall by three [handbreadths] and from that wall by three [handbreadths]. And if it had taught that the large [courtyard] is much wider, we would have learned from it even more clearly that it is prohibited due to the separation. And it cannot be said that the Tanna was precise with the measurements to teach us that only with this is it prohibited, and with less than this it is not, for with [a large courtyard of] ten [cubits] and four handbreadths it would also be prohibited, such as where it is separated by half a handbreadth on this side and by three and a half on that side, where the large [courtyard] is permitted with a remnant of any amount on this side and three and a half on that side, and the small [courtyard] is prohibited, since there is not lavud on both sides.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:5:1.hebrew: אלא לאו ש"מ - על כרחך, דוקא שלשה מכאן ושלשה מכאן למשרייה לגדולה נקט לה; ואפ"ה קטנה אסורה, דנראה מבחוץ לא מהני. ש"מ:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:5:1.english: Rather, can we not conclude from this - Perforce, [the baraita] specifically formulated [the case with] three [handbreadths] from here and three from there in order to permit the large [courtyard]; and even so, the small [courtyard] is prohibited, because [a post that is] visible from the outside is not effective. Conclude from this.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:6:1.hebrew: לא שמיע לי הא שמעתא - דרבה בר רב הונא מרב הונא אבוה, דנראה מבחוץ נידון משום לחי:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:6:1.english: I have not heard this teaching - [The teaching] of Rabba bar Rav Huna from Rav Huna, his father, that [a side post that is] visible from the outside is judged as a side post.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:7:1.hebrew: לחי המושך עם דופנו של מבוי - לחוץ, שנראה כמאריך את דופן המבוי, שמעמיד חודו כנגד עובי הדופן, דמיכסי חודו בעוביו של דופן, דשוה מבפנים, ונראה מבחוץ, שאין חודו של לחי מכסה כל עובי הדופן, שרחב ממנו:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:7:1.english: A side post that extends along the wall of an alleyway - [Extending] outward, such that it appears to extend the wall of the alleyway, for he places its edge against the thickness of the wall, so that its edge is covered by the thickness of the wall, [rendering it] even from the inside, and [yet it is] visible from the outside, because the edge of the side post does not cover the entire thickness of the wall, which is wider than it.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:7:2.hebrew: בכולו - בכל המבוי, שהרי אין כאן לחי:
Rashi on Eruvin 10a:7:2.english: In all of it - Throughout the entire alleyway, for there is no side post here.

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:8:1.english: Learn from it [that] the length of an alleyway is four [cubits] - From that which he said: "It is considered an alleyway."

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:8:2.english: [The area] between the side posts is forbidden - From the fact that he said: "Up to its inner edge."

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:8:3.english: And learn from it: [A side post that is] visible from the outside and even from the inside is judged as a side post - From the fact that he said: "It is judged as a side post."

Rashi on Eruvin 10a:9:1.english: [Can there be] a refutation and the halakha? - For we refuted it from [the case of] a small courtyard that was breached into a large one.

Tosafot on Eruvin 10a:1:1.hebrew: רבי היא דאמר בעינן שני פסין דתניא וכו' - משמע, לרבנן, אפילו בחצר מרובעת סגי בפס משהו, דבמרובעת פליגי, כמו שאפרש לקמן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 10a:1:1.english: It is Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who said we require two posts, as it was taught, etc. - This implies that according to the Rabbis, even in a square courtyard a post of any [minimal] size is sufficient, for it is regarding a square [courtyard] that they disagree, as I will explain below.

Tosafot on Eruvin 10a:4:1.hebrew: ושני טפחים סגי - האי ב' טפחים לאו דוקא, דהא אמרינן (לקמן עירובין ד' יב.): בשתי רוחות, משהו לכאן ומשהו לכאן. ואין סברא לומר דמשהו לאו דוקא, כדאמרינן פרק חלון (לקמן עירובין ד' פ.) גבי שיתופי מבואות: וצריך להגביה כל שהוא, וכמה כל שהוא? טפח; דאם כן, הוה ליה לפרושי כי התם. אי נמי: בפס גמור סגי בשני משהויין, אבל כותל עצמו לא חשיב פס אם לא ברוחב טפח, דאין היכר כל כך בכותל כמו בפס גמור:
Tosafot on Eruvin 10a:4:1.english: And two handbreadths suffice - This [mention of] two handbreadths is not exact, for behold, we say below (Eruvin 12a): [If there are upright boards] on two sides, a minimal amount here and a minimal amount there [suffices]. And it is not reasonable to say that "a minimal amount" is not exact, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Challon (below, Eruvin 80a) regarding the merging of alleyways: "And it is necessary to raise [the partnership food] any amount; and how much is any amount? A handbreadth"—for if so, it should have specified [it here] as it did there. Alternatively, in the case of an actual upright board, two minimal amounts suffice; but the wall itself is not considered an upright board unless it has a width of a handbreadth, because there is not as much of a noticeable distinction in a wall as there is in an actual upright board.
